h1: Buri Siri Boutique Hotel — a colonial boutique on a quiet soi in the heart of Nimmanhaemin
intro: Picture a hotel tucked away on a small soi, just a few steps from the bustle of Nimmanhaemin Road — step out the front gate and you're at the coffee shops, cafes and the big mall, yet you come back to sleep in a room so quiet and leafy it feels like another world · Buri Siri Boutique Hotel is a 4-star boutique that blends a colonial architectural feel with contemporary design and pulls it off nicely · 73 rooms and suites, a garden saltwater pool and a stylish bistro bar · from about ฿1,500/night · an average score of 8.6 from over 1,000 real reviews.

body.html: When you talk about the district where younger travelers, international visitors and digital nomads most often choose to stay in Chiang Mai, the name Nimmanhaemin tends to come up near the top — and in this district packed with cafes, restaurants and shopping malls, Buri Siri Boutique Hotel has placed itself in an interesting spot: on Sirimangkalajarn Soi 9, a small side soi that branches off the busy main road · The upshot is that you get a central location where you can walk almost anywhere, while not having to put up with traffic noise or late-night bar and pub noise · Plenty of people who've stayed in Nimman before and complained about noise are often surprised to find this soi much quieter than they expected, and that's the first selling point that puts this hotel on the radar of anyone who wants both convenience and calm at the same time.

Who is this hotel for? Going by the real reviews, Buri Siri suits couples who want a romantic feel without paying too much · people here to work, or digital nomads who want a place near the cafes with a co-working space · plus city-break travelers who like to wake up, walk to the shops, sip coffee and come back to a quiet room · As for families with small children or large groups needing lots of connecting rooms, you may want to look at other options too, because this hotel leans toward a calm boutique atmosphere rather than a family resort feel · If you plan to spend most of your time in Nimman — walking around to eat and shop, and only using a car for temple or mountain trips — this place fits that lifestyle perfectly.

Location and getting around is one of Buri Siri's strongest points · From the hotel it's a few minutes' walk to Nimman's well-known cafes and restaurants, a little farther to One Nimman, the colonial-style community mall that's a landmark of the district, and to Maya Lifestyle Shopping Center, a big mall with restaurants, a cinema and a supermarket · People who like to walk will be very happy here, since you barely need to call a car during the day · If you're heading to the Old City, Tha Phae Gate or the Sunday Walking Street, those are roughly a 10–15 min drive by Grab or songthaew (red truck) · Chiang Mai Airport (CNX) is about a 15 min drive away, which is very close for anyone who has just flown in and wants to get to their room quickly · One small note: the entrance soi is fairly narrow, so if you arrive in a large private car you may need to ease in slowly, but the hotel has free parking on site.

The rooms and decor are what make Buri Siri look more expensive than it actually is · The building and interiors use a colonial-meets-contemporary concept, with clean cream-white tones set against wooden furniture and wrought-iron detailing, for a classic feel that doesn't feel stuffy · There are 73 rooms in total across several tiers, starting with the Standard Twin at about 20 sqm for budget-minded guests, up to the Deluxe Studio in both king and twin layouts at about 42 sqm, which is very roomy and comfortable, and the Honeymoon Suite at about 49 sqm that suits couples · Most of the real reviews praise the rooms as clean, the beds comfortable, and the bathrooms spacious with a good, strong hot shower · A few mention that some rooms are starting to look a bit dated with the hotel's age, but overall they're still good value and give a genuine boutique feel rather than a generic chain-hotel room.

"The studio room was much bigger than I expected. I'd wake up, open the curtains to a green garden, and it was so quiet I'd forget I was in the middle of Nimman — and a five-minute walk out, there were cafes everywhere."

Facilities, the pool and the spa here are sized just right for a boutique — not resort-sized, but everything you need to relax · The highlight people mention most is the garden saltwater pool, which doesn't use chlorine like a regular pool, so it doesn't sting the eyes and is gentler on the skin · The pool sits in the middle of a lush green garden with sun loungers to lounge on, a leafy setting that's perfect for an afternoon dip or some photos · Many real reviews rate the pool as their favorite part of the hotel · There's also a small massage/spa room for a relaxing massage after a full day of sightseeing, plus a co-working space for people who need to sit and work — which appeals to the digital nomads who already favor Nimman · There's free Wi-Fi throughout the hotel, luggage storage, and a desk that helps with tours and arranging cars.

Food and drink at Buri Siri is handled by Buristro Bar & Café, which is a restaurant, cafe and bar all in one · It serves Thai food and cocktails in a laid-back setting, ideal for an evening drink after a day out · As for breakfast, to be honest it's where the reviews split into two camps — some praise it as freshly made and decent, but quite a few say the choices are limited and not as varied as you'd get at a hotel of this size · The upside is that the hotel sits in the middle of Chiang Mai's best cafe district, so if the in-house breakfast isn't to your liking, a few minutes' walk gets you to no end of top-notch coffee shops and brunch spots, which means breakfast isn't a big problem for anyone who likes to head out and find their own food.

On service, the hotel is generally praised for being friendly and helpful · Many of the staff speak English, and some can communicate in Chinese too, which helps international travelers a lot · Real reviews often mention staff who are cheerful, happy to recommend restaurants, call cars and handle check-in and check-out smoothly · That said, some reviews note that front-desk service isn't always consistent — at busy times, for instance, you may wait a little longer · This is the kind of thing you find at mid-size boutique hotels generally, and it doesn't go so far as to spoil the overall experience · The overall picture is warm, friendly service, fitting for a boutique that looks after guests with more care than a big chain hotel.

What real reviews say — both praise and gripes · On the praise side, most people make the location the star, since you can easily walk to Nimman, Maya and One Nimman while still being on a quiet soi · The garden saltwater pool scores high on likability · Rooms are clean, beds comfortable, and the colonial design gives a boutique feel that's good value · Staff are friendly and helpful · On the gripe side, the most common are that soundproofing between rooms isn't great — you can sometimes hear the room next door or the corridor · breakfast has limited choices · some rooms are starting to look dated with age · and front-desk service isn't always consistent at certain times · On balance, most of the gripes are acceptable given the price and location, while the praise covers the main factors people choose a Nimman hotel for in the first place.

Price and value · Buri Siri positions itself as an attainable, mid-priced 4-star boutique · Prices start at about ฿1,500/night for a Standard room at regular rates, rising to around ฿2,500–฿3,500/night for the Deluxe Studio and Honeymoon Suite, especially in high season · Compared with Nimman hotels of similar location and design, Buri Siri's prices are good value, especially if you land a studio room as large as 42 sqm at this price point, which is hard to find in the same district · What makes it even better value is the location, which helps you save on transport since you can walk to almost everything in the area · Our tip is to compare prices across several platforms — Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com — before you book, because rates can differ quite a bit by date and by site, and there are often good studio-room deals on certain days.

What to know before booking · One: if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a room deeper inside the building or on a higher floor, and request a quiet room in advance, since soundproofing between rooms is something many reviews mention · Two: if room space matters to you, go for a Deluxe Studio or above, because the Standard Twin at 20 sqm is fairly compact · Three: breakfast has limited choices, so if you're a serious breakfast person you might plan to head out to a cafe in the area instead, or check whether your booked package includes breakfast · Four: during Chiang Mai's high season (November–February), good rooms fill up fast, so book ahead and choose a free-cancellation rate to be safe · Five: the entrance soi is fairly narrow, so drive in slowly if you arrive in a large car; the hotel has free parking on site.

The Nimman district around the hotel is another reason people come back to stay again · Nimmanhaemin is known as one of the most cafe-dense districts in Chiang Mai — wake up, walk out of the soi, and within a few minutes you can choose from specialty coffee shops, brunch spots and pretty dessert cafes · At lunchtime there's a full range of Thai, Japanese and international restaurants · Come evening, the district turns into a hub of bars, chill-out spots and craft beer, and if you'd rather take a gentle stroll there's One Nimman, with its colonial styling, for photos and craft shopping · The key point is that Buri Siri is close enough to fully enjoy the district on foot, but once you head back into the soi you really do cut yourself off from the noise, giving you both daytime fun and nighttime calm — a mix that isn't easy to find in a popular tourist district like this.

A look at long-term value is worth considering for anyone staying several nights or here for a long work stint · Because Buri Siri has a co-working space and Wi-Fi that works throughout the hotel, plus a location ringed with cafes you can work in all day, digital nomads who need to be in Chiang Mai for weeks or months see this as a comfortable base · Booking a longer stay usually gets you a lower per-night rate, and you also save on transport since you barely need to call a car in the district · For people on a short 2–3 night trip to see Chiang Mai, it works well as a launch point for the Old City, Doi Suthep or the night markets, since calling a Grab from Nimman is easy and not expensive · Add up the room price, location and facilities, and Buri Siri makes for an overall high-value choice, especially compared with Nimman boutiques that charge more but offer similar room space and atmosphere.

Bottom line · Buri Siri Boutique Hotel is a well-judged choice for anyone who wants to stay in the heart of Nimmanhaemin in a calm boutique setting, without paying luxury-tier prices · Its clear strengths are a location within easy walking distance of cafes, Maya and One Nimman while still tucked away on a quiet soi, plus colonial design that looks better than the price, a garden saltwater pool that many people love, and friendly staff · The limitations you have to accept are soundproofing between rooms that isn't great, limited breakfast choices, and some rooms that are starting to show their age · If you're a couple, a digital nomad, or a city-break traveler who values location and atmosphere over top-tier luxury, this place is clearly worth the money, and it's one of the Nimman boutiques worth keeping an eye on whenever you're looking for somewhere to stay in Chiang Mai.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Buri Siri Boutique Hotel Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Buri Siri Boutique Hotel in Chiang Mai · what's nearby?
faq.a: Buri Siri is located on Sirimangkalajarn Soi 9 in the heart of Nimmanhaemin · about a 5 min walk to One Nimman and 7 min to Maya mall · the district's cafe and restaurant streets are just a 1–3 min walk away · the Old City and Tha Phae Gate are about a 12 min drive · Chiang Mai Airport about 15 min.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Buri Siri · what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿1,500/night for a Standard Twin (20 sqm) · the Deluxe Studio in both king and twin (42 sqm) is around ฿2,500 · the Honeymoon Suite (49 sqm) around ฿3,500 · prices depend on the dates and platform, so compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Who is Buri Siri best suited to?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, digital nomads and city-break travelers who want to stay in the heart of Nimman in a calm boutique setting · there's a co-working space and it's close to the cafes · it leans on location and design over top-tier luxury, so large families needing lots of connecting rooms may want to look at other options too.

faq.q: What's the pool like at Buri Siri?
faq.a: It's an outdoor saltwater pool in the garden with no chlorine, so it doesn't sting the eyes and is gentler on the skin than a regular pool · set in a lush green garden with sun loungers, it's one of the spots real reviews like most.

faq.q: What downsides should you know about before booking Buri Siri?
faq.a: From the real reviews, the most common are that soundproofing between rooms isn't great — you may hear the room next door · breakfast has limited choices · some rooms are starting to look dated · and front-desk service isn't always consistent at certain times — we'd suggest asking for a quiet room deep inside and choosing a studio room or above.

faq.q: How far ahead should you book · can you cancel?
faq.a: For high season (November–February) you should book 4–6 weeks ahead, since Nimman is popular and good rooms fill up fast · every platform usually has a free-cancellation option — choose that if your plans aren't set yet.
